subject: GPU burst-queue incident & customer sync: QuantFlow dedicated pool
messages:
From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@quantflow.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: support@quantflow.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High error rates and queue backlog on our dedicated pool right now

Olga,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 500 errors and timeouts from our production traffic to the dedicated pool you provisioned for us around 08:42 PT. Error rate spiked to ~18% and tail latency jumped to >8s for many requests. Our observability shows a rapid growth in the request queue (queued requests spiking) and a number of token-generation jobs being retried.

Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side capacity/autoscale issue or something specific to our workload? We're seeing impact on customer-facing features and would like immediate mitigation steps and ETA.

Quick context: QuantFlow is on "dedicated-g4-reserve-2" pool, Model pinned to rwinference/longform-13b:v3.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Platform Engineering
QuantFlow.ai

(attachment: gpu-queue-snapshot.png)

- Open an elevated incident channel and will keep you updated every 30 minutes until stabilized.

Marissa: please prepare customer-facing note and coordinate credits if we need to offer a service-level concession.

Subject: Re: High error rates and queue backlog on our dedicated pool right now

Quick technical summary from the serving team: 
- Root symptom: sudden burst of long-context requests from a subset of QuantFlow sessions caused continuous KV-cache growth and elongated per-token generation time. This increased per-request GPU time and reduced effective throughput, resulting in request queuing.
- Autoscaler behavior: the autoscaler observed higher utilization but did not trigger the expected scale-up due to a transient mis-evaluation of the node readiness metric (we missed a window where a small fraction of nodes reported degraded health, which suppressed the scale decision).
- Immediate mitigation applied at 09:30 PT: forced scale-up of two reserved nodes and enabled aggressive early-eviction for stale prefix caches on the pool. That reduced queue depth by ~65% within 3 minutes.

We've attached a concise timeline and a CSV snapshot of queue depth and error rates. (attachment: incident-timeline.csv)

Next steps: 
1) We will keep the two extra nodes up for 24 hours while we watch for regressions.
2) Postmortem investigating autoscaler decision logic, including the node-readiness gating and the interaction with KV cache retention.
3) Short-term config change: tweak the readiness thresholds so a 10% node-degraded signal won't block scale-up for customer-critical pools.

Rajesh — let us know if you want us to route a percentage of traffic to a warm standby now; otherwise we recommend keeping the pool at the elevated size while we complete verification.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Customer update: Incident mitigation & next steps

Rajesh — following up with a customer-facing summary you can share internally:

Summary (for QuantFlow leadership / ops):
- Impact window: 08:42 PT — 09:33 PT (primary impact); residual tail errors until ~09:48 PT for some requests.
- What happened: A burst of long-context generation tasks increased per-request GPU time, causing queueing and elevated error rates. The autoscaler did not scale during the initial spike due to a node-readiness gating issue.
- Immediate mitigation: Forced scale-up of two reserved nodes and cache eviction, restoring throughput and lowering error rate. We held the extra nodes and will monitor.
- Customer impact: Some live customer requests experienced elevated latency and retries; estimated % of impacted requests: ~6–9% of production traffic during the primary impact window.

Planned follow-ups:
- Internal postmortem to be shared by 2027-05-12 with root cause, timeline, and concrete code/config fixes.
- Offer: We will extend a credit equivalent to one week of dedicated capacity for the affected pool. If you prefer a different remedy (engineering support hours / technical deep-dive), let us know.
- Action: schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow (2027-05-10) to review the postmortem and discuss long-term guardrails (shard-level throttles, autoscale policy hardening).

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv, redwood-action-plan-v1.pdf

Thanks for your patience — we're treating this as a high priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
